questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) Cinnamon is a spice obtained from the inner bark of several tree species from the genus Cinnamomum. Cinnamon is made by cutting the stems of cinnamon trees. The inner bark is then extracted and the woody parts removed. When it dries, it forms strips that curl into rolls, called cinnamon sticks. These sticks can be ground to form cinnamon powder. The spice, consisting of the dried inner bark, is brown in colour and has a delicately fragrant aroma and a warm sweet flavour. The distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil and principal component, cinnamaldehyde, as well as numerous other constituents including eugenol.

(2) There are two main types of cinnamon: Cassia and Ceylon. The two have different nutritional profiles. Ceylon cinnamon comes from Sri Lanka. Some people call it "true cinnamon." Cassia cinnamon, on the other hand, originates from southern China. Cassia is cheaper than Ceylon cinnamon. Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, somewhat bitter flavour while Ceylon is sweeter and lighter in flavor.

(3) Cinnamon was once more valuable than gold. In Egypt it was sought for embalming and religious practices. In medieval Europe it was used for religious rites and as a flavouring agent. Later it was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade.

(4) Cinnamon is widely used as an aromatic condiment and flavouring additive in a wide variety of cuisines, sweet and savoury dishes, breakfast cereals, snack foods, bagels, teas, hot chocolate and traditional foods.

(5) Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years. In recent years, modern science has started to confirm many of the potential health benefits associated with cinnamon. Cinnamon has antimicrobial and antifungal properties, which is why it's often found in dental-hygiene products and is sold as cinnamon supplements. It is also a good source of antioxidants, substances that inhibit the effect of free radicals (reactive atoms that can damage cells). Due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is currently being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

(6) Studies also suggest that cinnamon has anti-diabetic properties, and may offer protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease, among other conditions. However, more evidence is needed to confirm cinnamon's benefits. In the short term, consuming moderate amounts of cinnamon as a spice or as a supplement seems to be safe for most people. However, cinnamon contains coumarin. This is a natural flavouring, but it also plays a role in creating warfarin, the common blood-thinning drug. Consuming too much coumarin can lead to liver damage and affect coagulation.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of ___________. Paragraph (1)
sub_questions.solution: According to Paragraph (1), the distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil whose principal component is cinnamaldehyde, along with other constituents such as eugenol. Therefore, the characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of cinnamaldehyde.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the reading of the passage, examine, in about 40 words, how cinnamon derived from the trees is made fit to be used as a spice. Paragraph (1)

key_points: Stems of cinnamon trees are cut
Inner bark is extracted and woody parts removed
The bark dries into curled strips called cinnamon sticks which can be ground into powder

sub_questions.solution: Cinnamon is made fit for use as a spice through a step-by-step process. First, the stems of cinnamon trees are cut. Then the inner bark is carefully extracted and the woody parts are removed. As it dries, the bark curls into rolls called cinnamon sticks, which can further be ground into cinnamon powder ready for use.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention one point of difference between Ceylon cinnamon and Cassia cinnamon. Paragraph (2)

key_points: Ceylon cinnamon has a sweeter and lighter flavour, whereas Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter flavour.

sub_questions.solution: One key difference is their flavour profile. Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter flavour, while Ceylon cinnamon is sweeter and lighter in flavour. Additionally, Cassia originates from southern China and is cheaper, while Ceylon comes from Sri Lanka and is often called 'true cinnamon.'

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The author says that cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because ___________. Paragraph (3)

fill_values: it was highly sought after for embalming and religious practices in Egypt, used for religious rites and as a flavouring agent in medieval Europe, and was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade

sub_questions.solution: The author says that cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because it was extremely valued across different civilisations — in Egypt it was used for embalming and religious practices, in medieval Europe for religious rites and flavouring, and it was the most profitable spice traded by the Dutch East India Company.

sub_questions.text_english:
What is the tone of the writer in the given lines from paragraph (5)? Rationalize your response in about 40 words.
"Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years."

key_points: The tone is informative and appreciative
The writer acknowledges cinnamon's long historical medicinal value
The use of 'prized' and 'thousands of years' reflects admiration and respect

sub_questions.solution: The tone of the writer in these lines is informative and appreciative. By using the word 'prized,' the author conveys a sense of admiration for cinnamon's enduring medicinal value. The phrase 'thousands of years' reinforces the idea that cinnamon's health benefits have been recognised and respected across human history.

sub_questions.text_english:
The writer's use of the phrases 'modern science has started to confirm' in paragraph (5) and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' in paragraph (6) suggests that the benefits of cinnamon are:
1. proven
2. scientific
3. uncertain
4. controversial
5. harmful
Select the correct option:
(A) 1 and 3
(B) 2 and 4
(C) only 3
(D) only 5
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) 'only 3 — uncertain' is correct. The phrase 'modern science has started to confirm' implies that confirmation is still in progress, and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' directly states that the benefits have not yet been fully proven. This makes the benefits uncertain, not proven, controversial, or harmful.

sub_questions.text_english:
Which of the following statements about cinnamon and its health benefits is true?
(A) Modern science has evidence to prove that cinnamon has many anti-diabetic properties, and it offers complete protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease.
(B) Cinnamon lacks antimicrobial and antifungal properties, making it unsuitable for dental hygiene products.
(C) Antioxidants found in cinnamon have no effect on free radicals in the body.
(D) Cinnamon's anti-inflammatory properties are being researched for its potential benefits in Alzheimer's disease, irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer. Paragraph (6)

options_english.A: Modern science has evidence to prove that cinnamon has many anti-diabetic properties, and it offers complete protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease.
options_english.B: Cinnamon lacks antimicrobial and antifungal properties, making it unsuitable for dental hygiene products.
options_english.C: Antioxidants found in cinnamon have no effect on free radicals in the body.
options_english.D: Cinnamon's anti-inflammatory properties are being researched for its potential benefits in Alzheimer's disease, irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

sub_questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Paragraph (5) clearly states that due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is currently being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer. Options A, B, and C directly contradict information stated in the passage.

sub_questions.text_english:
Which of the following statements best describes the author's attitude toward cinnamon and its uses?
(A) Finds cinnamon to be a prized condiment which can be used in almost all food items.
(B) Believes that cinnamon should be used by everyone, everyday.
(C) Recognizes that cinnamon has many useful properties, including health benefits.
(D) Believes that cinnamon should only be used as a medicinal supplement.

options_english.A: Finds cinnamon to be a prized condiment which can be used in almost all food items.
options_english.B: Believes that cinnamon should be used by everyone, everyday.
options_english.C: Recognizes that cinnamon has many useful properties, including health benefits.
options_english.D: Believes that cinnamon should only be used as a medicinal supplement.

sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Throughout the passage, the author discusses cinnamon's culinary uses, historical significance, and potential health benefits in a balanced and informative manner. The author neither restricts cinnamon to food use only nor prescribes it exclusively as medicine, but rather acknowledges its wide range of useful properties.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) When planning vacations, Indians typically prioritize domestic destinations, as shown by Ministry of Tourism data indicating 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India compared to 21 million international departures in 2022. Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka stand out as the top states for domestic tourism. Reasons for domestic tourism are many, some travel because it suits their budget while others love to explore the historical, cultural diversity. The government today is focussing on tourist-friendly infrastructure which is making travel more convenient for the domestic traveller.

(2) In terms of outbound tourism, a significant proportion of Indian travellers, totalling 5.9 million, visited the United Arab Emirates in 2022, comprising 28 percent of total outbound tourist travel. Other Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait also rank among the top destinations, with 2.4 million, 880,000, and 830,000 Indian visitors, respectively. Additionally, countries like the United States and the United Kingdom attract a considerable number of Indian tourists because these countries offer a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences along with enjoying unique cuisines and diverse landscapes.

(3) The popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends. The current issue of the International Organization for Migration's (IOM) World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia. For instance, the Emirates hosted approximately 3.6 million Indian migrants as of August 2023. Only via two corridors have more people transferred from one country to another as of 2020 according to the IOM: Mexico to the United States with around 11 million and Syria to Turkey with approximately 4 million. These migration corridors rank among the top ten globally.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
What does the use of the phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' by the writer, in paragraph (1) imply?
(A) Indian tourists prefer places in the country itself.
(B) Indian tourists like to stay at home.
(C) Indian tourists mainly travel on low budgets.
(D) Indian tourists love to hitch-hike and trek.

options_english.A: Indian tourists prefer places in the country itself.
options_english.B: Indian tourists like to stay at home.
options_english.C: Indian tourists mainly travel on low budgets.
options_english.D: Indian tourists love to hitch-hike and trek.

sub_questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. The phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' means that Indian tourists prefer to travel within India rather than going abroad. This is supported by the Ministry of Tourism data showing 1.7 billion domestic visits compared to only 21 million international departures. The other options either misrepresent the meaning or introduce ideas not stated in the passage.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate option from those given in brackets, based on your understanding of paragraph (2).
The statement that, World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia, is a/an ________ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an __________ (subjective judgement/objective detail).
sub_questions.solution: The statement is a fact because it is an objective detail. It is drawn from the IOM's World Migration Report, which is a credible, data-based source. The information reports verifiable migration flows and is not based on personal opinion or subjective judgement, making it a factual and objective statement.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw a comparative analysis of domestic tourists travelling within India with domestic tourists travelling outside India in 2022. Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India in 2022
Only 21 million international departures in 2022
The gap shows Indians strongly prefer travelling within the country

sub_questions.solution: In 2022, a massive 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits were recorded within India, whereas only 21 million Indians travelled abroad. This stark contrast shows that domestic tourism is far more popular among Indians. Budget considerations, cultural curiosity, and improved government infrastructure make travel within India far more preferred than international tourism.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following with a suitable reason. Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians _________.

fill_values: due to significant migration trends, as many Indians have settled or work in the Gulf states, making them popular travel destinations

sub_questions.solution: Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians because of strong migration connections. A large number of Indian migrants live and work in countries like the UAE and Saudi Arabia. As of August 2023, the Emirates alone hosted approximately 3.6 million Indian migrants, naturally making these destinations attractive for Indian travellers visiting family and friends.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that is true for the Assertion and Reason given below:
Assertion: Indians prioritize Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh for domestic tourism.
Reason: These states are full of historical monuments.
(A) Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
(B) Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
(C) The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
(D) The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

options_english.A: Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.B: Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.C: The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options_english.D: The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The Assertion is true — the passage mentions Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh as top domestic tourism destinations. The Reason may also be generally true, but the passage does not specifically cite historical monuments as the reason. The passage mentions budget suitability and cultural diversity as reasons, making the Reason an incomplete and not the correct explanation.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The fourthmost visited outbound destination for Indians to the Gulf is _________.
sub_questions.solution: According to Paragraph (2), among Gulf destinations, the UAE ranked first with 5.9 million Indian visitors, Saudi Arabia second with 2.4 million, Qatar third with 880,000, and Kuwait fourth with 830,000 Indian visitors. Therefore, the fourth most visited outbound destination for Indians to the Gulf is Kuwait.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two reasons for domestic tourism becoming popular.

key_points: Budget suitability — domestic travel is more affordable
Desire to explore India's historical and cultural diversity

sub_questions.solution: Two reasons for the growing popularity of domestic tourism in India are: first, it suits the budget of many travellers as it is far more affordable than international travel; and second, many Indians love to explore the rich historical and cultural diversity that the country's various states and regions offer.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the writer's view about the tourism industry in the west? Write any two points.

key_points: Western countries like the US and UK offer a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences
They attract Indian tourists with unique cuisines and diverse landscapes

sub_questions.solution: The writer views the tourism industry in the west as diverse and attractive. Two points the writer highlights are: first, countries like the United States and the United Kingdom offer a blend of traditional and contemporary experiences; and second, they attract Indian tourists with their unique cuisines and diverse and varied landscapes.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the word in paragraph (3) that indicates the 'preference' of people travelling to the Gulf.

key_points: popularity

sub_questions.solution: The word in Paragraph (3) that indicates the 'preference' of people travelling to the Gulf is 'popularity.' The paragraph begins with the statement 'The popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends,' clearly indicating that these destinations are preferred or favoured by Indian travellers.

questions.text_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed.
questions.instruction_line_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed. (10×1=10)
questions.solution: Grammar task set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter.
I believe that with your support and ________ (cooperate), we can find a mutually agreeable solution that meets the expectations of all stakeholders involved.
sub_questions.solution: The correct form is 'cooperation.' The word is a noun and is required here because it follows the conjunction 'and' alongside another noun 'support.' The verb 'cooperate' must be converted into its noun form using the suffix '-tion,' giving us 'cooperation.' Full sentence: I believe that with your support and cooperation, we can find a mutually agreeable solution.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the given sentence from an electric cooker's instruction manual. Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence.
For avoid damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.
Use the given format for your response.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of 'avoid' after the preposition 'For.' The rule is that a preposition must be followed by a gerund (verb+ing form), not the base form of a verb. Therefore, 'avoid' should be corrected to 'avoiding.' Corrected sentence: For avoiding damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.

sub_questions.text_english:
Amit and Pallavi had a conversation about the inauguration of Pallavi's event. Report Amit's question.
Did you manage to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the next month?

key_points: Amit asked Pallavi if she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month.

sub_questions.solution: Amit asked Pallavi if she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month. In reported speech, the question word 'Did' is replaced by 'if,' the subject 'you' changes to 'she,' the verb 'manage' changes to 'had managed,' and 'next month' changes to 'the following month' to reflect the time shift.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the dialogue between Bharti and her mother, Geeta, regarding Geeta's birthday plans.
Bharti: Do you want to go to a hill station on your birthday?
Geeta: No, I want to stay at home and call my friends over.
Select the correct option that reports the above dialogue.
Bharti asked Geeta if she wanted to go to a hill station on her birthday. Geeta replied in the negative and said that __________.
(A) she wanted to stay home and call her friends for celebrating.
(B) I wanted to stay home and call my friends to celebrate.
(C) she wanted to stay at home and call her friends over.
(D) she wants to stay home by calling her friends to celebrate.

options_english.A: she wanted to stay home and call her friends for celebrating.
options_english.B: I wanted to stay home and call my friends to celebrate.
options_english.C: she wanted to stay at home and call her friends over.
options_english.D: she wants to stay home by calling her friends to celebrate.

sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. In reported speech, 'I' changes to 'she,' 'want' changes to 'wanted' (backshift of tense), and the rest of the sentence retains the original meaning. Option (A) changes the meaning, (B) incorrectly retains first person, and (D) uses present tense incorrectly and changes the structure. Option (C) accurately reflects both meaning and grammar.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the line of a notice placed on the notice board of a company.
Please be informed that there will be a staff meeting in the conference room on Friday, 7th June, at 10:00 a.m. It is __________ for all to attend. (mandatory/obligatory/indispensable)
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'mandatory.' In the context of an official company notice requiring attendance at a meeting, 'mandatory' is the most precise and formal word. It means 'required by law or rules.' While 'obligatory' is also acceptable, 'mandatory' is more standard in formal workplace notices. 'Indispensable' means absolutely necessary and refers to things, not attendance. Full sentence: It is mandatory for all to attend.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply correction for the given sentence from a preface of a book.
Writing this book have been a journey of exploration and discovery.
Use the given format for your response.
sub_questions.solution: The error is 'have.' The subject of the sentence is the gerund phrase 'Writing this book,' which acts as a singular subject. Singular subjects require singular verbs, so 'have' must be corrected to 'has.' Corrected sentence: Writing this book has been a journey of exploration and discovery.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from an analytical paragraph.
The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connected people across the globe in unprecedented ways.
(A) has → have
(B) communication → communicating
(C) connected → connecting
(D) in → for
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The error is 'connected,' which should be 'connecting.' After the preposition 'by,' a gerund (verb+ing form) is required to show the means by which something is done. 'Connected' is a past participle and is grammatically incorrect here. The corrected sentence reads: The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connecting people across the globe in unprecedented ways.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the given entry in a personal diary, by filling the blank with the correct option.
Today was a rollercoaster of emotions. It started off with a sense of excitement and anticipation as I __________ on a new project at work.
(A) embarking
(B) embark
(C) embarked
(D) have embarked
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) 'embarked' is correct. The diary entry is written in the simple past tense as indicated by 'Today was' and 'It started off.' Therefore, the verb in the blank must also be in the simple past tense. 'Embarked' is the simple past form of 'embark.' Options (A) and (B) are wrong forms, and (D) changes the tense unnecessarily to present perfect.

sub_questions.text_english:
Report the dialogue between a salesman and his customer, by completing the sentence.
Salesman: I have a wide range of sportswear.
Customer: Please show me something in cotton fabric, which is suitable for summers.
The salesman stated ____________. The customer requested the salesman to show something in cotton fabric which would be suitable for summers.

fill_values: that he had a wide range of sportswear

sub_questions.solution: The correct reported form is: 'that he had a wide range of sportswear.' In reported speech, 'I' changes to 'he,' 'have' changes to 'had' (tense backshift from present to past), and the conjunction 'that' is added. Full reported sentence: The salesman stated that he had a wide range of sportswear. The customer requested the salesman to show something in cotton fabric which would be suitable for summers.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete an announcement on a flight.
In thirty minutes, our flight attendants ________ meal service.
(A) will began
(B) will begin
(C) should begin
(D) can begin
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'will begin' is correct. This is an official flight announcement about a future action that is certain and scheduled to happen. The simple future tense 'will + base verb' is appropriate here. Option (A) 'will began' is grammatically incorrect as 'began' is past tense. Options (C) and (D) introduce unnecessary uncertainty with modal verbs 'should' and 'can.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the line from a 'Save the Environment' song, by filling the blank with the correct option.
Pollution, pollution, its time to take a stand,
for the health of our planet, we've got to lend a hand,
Reduce, reuse, recycle, that's the key,
________ our world for you and me.
(A) for preserve
(B) to preserve
(C) to preserved
(D) for preserved
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'to preserve' is correct. The infinitive 'to + base verb' is used here to express purpose — the reason for reducing, reusing, and recycling is to preserve our world. 'For + gerund' is grammatically possible to express purpose, but 'for preserve' is incorrect because 'preserve' is not a gerund. Options (C) and (D) incorrectly use 'preserved' (past participle) after 'to' and 'for.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the following instruction put up for safe use of elevators.
Please refrain by standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.
Use the given format for your response.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the preposition 'by.' The correct collocation is 'refrain from,' not 'refrain by.' The verb 'refrain' always takes the preposition 'from' before a gerund to mean 'to stop oneself from doing something.' Corrected sentence: Please refrain from standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.

sub_questions.text_english: As Kavita/Rohit Ranjan of Sooraj Apartments, Roshan Nagar, you feel that the increasing noise levels from construction activities, traffic and loud gatherings are disrupting the peace and tranquility of your neighbourhood. This is particularly problematic during late hours and is impacting the sleep and well-being of residents. Write a letter to the DM of your city area, in about 120 words, stating the problem and requesting him to take necessary action for controlling the problem of noise. Give suitable suggestions.

key_points: Sender's address, date, and designation of the addressee (DM)
Subject line clearly stating the noise pollution problem
Description of the problem — construction, traffic, loud gatherings, especially at late hours
Impact on residents — disturbed sleep and deteriorating well-being
Specific suggestions such as imposing noise curfews, restricting construction timings, and holding gatherings accountable
Polite closing with a request for prompt action

sub_questions.solution:
Sooraj Apartments,
Roshan Nagar,
[City]
Date: 7th June, 2026

The District Magistrate,
[City Administration Office]

Subject: Request to Control Rising Noise Pollution in Roshan Nagar

Respected Sir/Madam,

I, Rohit Ranjan, a resident of Sooraj Apartments, Roshan Nagar, write to bring to your attention the alarming rise in noise levels in our neighbourhood. Construction activities, heavy traffic, and loud late-night gatherings have severely disrupted the peace and tranquility of our locality. Residents, including elderly citizens and young children, are suffering from sleep deprivation and deteriorating health.

I humbly request you to impose strict time restrictions on construction work, enforce noise-limit regulations for vehicles, and penalise those hosting loud gatherings after 10 p.m. Prompt action on your part will greatly improve the quality of life in our neighbourhood.

Yours sincerely,
Rohit Ranjan

sub_questions.text_english: You are Suman/Sujit, an active member of your society's "Save the Climate" club. You reside at 786, Hawa Colony, Saafbagh. You feel concerned about the pressing problem of climate change and the urgent need for immediate action. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, in about 120 words, suggesting measures to advocate sustainable practices in the community.

key_points: Sender's address, date, and salutation to The Editor
Subject line about climate change and sustainable practices
Brief statement of concern — urgency of climate change
Suggestion 1 — promoting renewable energy sources
Suggestion 2 — reducing plastic use and encouraging recycling
Suggestion 3 — community tree-plantation drives and carpooling
Polite closing

sub_questions.solution:
786, Hawa Colony,
Saafbagh,
[City]
Date: 7th June, 2026

The Editor,
[Name of National Daily]

Subject: Advocating Sustainable Practices to Combat Climate Change

Dear Sir/Madam,

Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw public attention to the urgent crisis of climate change. As a member of our society's Save the Climate club, I strongly believe that immediate community-level action is essential.

I would like to suggest the following measures: residents should adopt renewable energy sources such as solar panels; single-use plastics must be replaced with reusable alternatives; community tree-plantation drives should be organised regularly; and carpooling should be encouraged to reduce vehicular emissions.

Small, collective steps taken today can make a significant difference for future generations. I urge citizens to act responsibly.

Yours sincerely,
Sujit

questions.text_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below.
questions.solution: Analytical paragraph writing task. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Natural food, typically refers to food that has not been processed or preserved in any significant way before it is consumed, while ultra-processed food refers to food items that have been altered from their natural state through various methods. Given below is a table that differentiates between natural and processed foods. Study the description given and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, drawing a comparison between the two:
Natural Food: High fibre, Healthy nutrients, Healthy fats, Low sodium, Regulates blood sugar, blood pressure and provides healthy nutrients.
Processed Food: High sugar, Unhealthy nutrients, Unhealthy fats, High sodium, Tasty, ready to eat and addictive.

key_points: Introduction defining both natural and processed food
Contrast in nutritional content — fibre vs sugar, healthy vs unhealthy nutrients
Contrast in fat and sodium content
Health benefits of natural food vs addictive nature of processed food
Conclusion recommending natural food

sub_questions.solution: Natural food and processed food represent two contrasting approaches to nourishment. Natural food, which is consumed without significant alteration, is rich in fibre, healthy nutrients, and healthy fats, and contains low sodium. It helps regulate blood sugar and blood pressure, thereby promoting overall well-being. Processed food, on the other hand, undergoes various modifications that strip it of its nutritional value. It is high in sugar, unhealthy fats, and sodium, and contains harmful additives. While processed food may be tasty, convenient, and ready to eat, its addictive nature makes people consume more than necessary, leading to lifestyle diseases such as diabetes, obesity, and hypertension. Thus, although processed food offers convenience, natural food is far superior in promoting long-term health and should be preferred in daily diets.

sub_questions.text_english:
Social Media has a lasting impact on our thought process and influences our thinking in both positive and negative ways. With the help of the given cues and using your own ideas, write an analytical paragraph on 'The Impact of Social Media on Teenagers' in about 120 words.
POSITIVE: connects peers, creative expression, access information, community building.
NEGATIVE: impacts self-esteem, cyber bullying, privacy intrusion, distraction and addiction.

key_points: Introduction acknowledging social media's dual impact on teenagers
Positive impacts — peer connection, creative expression, access to information, community building
Negative impacts — reduced self-esteem, cyberbullying, privacy concerns, addiction and distraction
Balanced conclusion suggesting responsible use

sub_questions.solution: Social media has become an inseparable part of a teenager's life, shaping their thinking and behaviour in profound ways. On the positive side, it helps teenagers connect with peers, express their creativity through art and writing, access vast amounts of information, and build supportive communities around shared interests. These benefits can foster confidence, learning, and a sense of belonging. However, the negative impacts are equally significant. Overexposure to idealized images on social media can damage teenagers' self-esteem. Cyberbullying has emerged as a serious concern, causing emotional distress. Privacy intrusion by unknown individuals and platforms poses safety risks. Furthermore, excessive use leads to addiction and distraction from studies and real-life relationships. Therefore, teenagers must be encouraged to use social media responsibly and with awareness of its consequences.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Extract-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (a): He felt certain that his wings would never support him; so he bent his head and ran away back to the little hole under the ledge where he slept at night. Even when each of his brothers and his little sister, whose wings were far shorter than his own, ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away, he failed to muster up courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate. His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away. But for the life of him he could not move.
(Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)

State any one inference about the parents of the baby seagull from the given statement: 'His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away.'

key_points: The parents were determined to push the young seagull to overcome his fear and learn to fly, using tough love as a strategy.

sub_questions.solution: One inference about the parents of the baby seagull is that they were deeply determined and used tough love as a parenting strategy. By calling shrilly, scolding him, and threatening to let him starve, they showed they were not willing to give up on him and firmly believed that pushing him to the edge was the only way to make him fly.

sub_questions.text_english: Where did the little seagull sleep at night?

key_points: The little seagull slept at night in a little hole under the ledge.

sub_questions.solution: The little seagull slept at night in a small hole under the ledge. When he felt afraid and could not muster the courage to fly, he would bend his head and run back to this little hole, which served as his place of safety and comfort.

sub_questions.text_english: Which factors contributed to the young seagull's reluctance to fly despite the encouragement and threats from his parents? Elaborate in about 40 words, with reference to the extract.

key_points: Deep fear and self-doubt — he felt certain his wings would not support him
The vast expanse below appeared dangerously desperate to him
Even seeing his siblings fly could not overcome his overwhelming fear

sub_questions.solution: The young seagull's reluctance to fly was primarily caused by deep-seated fear and self-doubt. He was convinced that his wings would never be strong enough to support him. The plunge downward appeared desperately dangerous. Even seeing his siblings, who had shorter wings, fly successfully could not overpower his overwhelming sense of dread and insecurity.

sub_questions.text_english:
Which phrase or word would correctly substitute 'muster up' in the given sentence from the extract?
He failed to 'muster up' courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate.
(A) review
(B) resolve
(C) distribute
(D) gather
sub_questions.solution: Option (D) 'gather' is correct. 'Muster up' means to collect or summon something, especially an emotion or quality such as courage. The closest synonym in this context is 'gather,' as in 'gather courage.' Option (A) 'review' means to look over; (B) 'resolve' means to decide; and (C) 'distribute' means to spread out — none of these match the meaning of 'muster up.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (b): Tricki was tottering along in his little tweed coat.... He struggled on, drooping in his harness. I thought it wouldn't be long before I heard from Mrs. Pumphrey. The expected call came within a few days. Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing. Refused even his favourite dishes; and besides, he had bouts of vomiting. He spent all his time lying on a rug, panting. Didn't want to go for walks, didn't want to do anything. I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalized for about a fortnight to be kept under observation. The poor lady almost swooned. She was sure he would pine and die if he did not see her every day. But I took a firm line. Tricki was very ill and this was the only way to save him.
(A Triumph of Surgery)

Why had the author made his plans in advance?
(A) Mrs. Pumphrey was worried that Tricki would pine and die without her.
(B) The author was aware of the severity of Tricki's medical condition.
(C) The author knew about Mrs. Pumphrey's financial condition.
(D) The author had planned his own vacation.

options_english.A: Mrs. Pumphrey was worried that Tricki would pine and die without her.
options_english.B: The author was aware of the severity of Tricki's medical condition.
options_english.C: The author knew about Mrs. Pumphrey's financial condition.
options_english.D: The author had planned his own vacation.

sub_questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The author (the vet) had already observed Tricki's worsening condition — the dog was tottering, drooping, and visibly ill. Having assessed the severity of Tricki's medical condition, the author anticipated the call from Mrs. Pumphrey and made his plans in advance. Options A, C, and D are not supported by the text.

sub_questions.text_english: The author firmly proposed the need to remove Tricki from the house for a specified period. Elaborate the reason for doing so in about 40 words.

key_points: Tricki was severely ill — refusing food, vomiting, and lethargic
Mrs. Pumphrey's excessive pampering was the root cause of his illness
Removing him from the house was the only way to treat him properly under medical observation

sub_questions.solution: The author proposed removing Tricki from the house because the dog's condition had deteriorated severely due to Mrs. Pumphrey's over-indulgence. Tricki refused food, vomited frequently, and lay helplessly on a rug all day. The author knew that only by removing him from his pampered environment and placing him under strict medical observation could he recover and regain his health.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank with the correct word from the brackets.
The word 'swooned' in the following sentence indicates almost ________ (tripped/fainted).
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'fainted.' The word 'swooned' means to faint, typically from shock, strong emotion, or distress. In the extract, Mrs. Pumphrey almost swooned upon hearing the suggestion that Tricki be hospitalized for a fortnight. This physical reaction indicates the extreme distress she felt at the thought of being separated from her beloved dog.

sub_questions.text_english: "Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught." What does this suggest about her character? Mention any one reason.

key_points: It suggests that Mrs. Pumphrey was excessively attached to Tricki and deeply emotional about his well-being.

sub_questions.solution: The statement 'Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught' suggests that she was excessively and emotionally attached to Tricki. Her being distraught merely because her pet was ill reveals her over-indulgent and highly sensitive character. She treated Tricki not as a pet but as her entire world, which was also the root cause of the dog's deteriorating health.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Poetry extract-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (a): Some say the world will end in fire / Some say in ice. / From what I've tasted of desire / I hold with those who favour fire. (Fire and Ice)

The speaker offers evidence to support his preference for one theory over the other. Mention the evidence.

key_points: The speaker's personal experience of desire — 'From what I've tasted of desire' — is the evidence he offers to support his belief that fire will end the world.

sub_questions.solution: The evidence the speaker offers to support his preference for fire is his personal experience with desire. He says 'From what I've tasted of desire,' implying that he has experienced the intense, consuming nature of desire, which he compares to fire. This lived experience of passionate, destructive emotion convinces him that the world is more likely to end in fire.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the prediction of the poet about how the world will come to an end? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: The poet believes fire will cause the end of the world
Fire symbolises human desire and passion
The poet also acknowledges ice (hatred and indifference) could destroy the world if it were to end twice

sub_questions.solution: The poet Robert Frost predicts that the world will most likely end in fire, which symbolises burning human desire and passion. He has personally experienced the consuming power of desire. However, he also acknowledges that ice, representing hatred and cold indifference, is equally powerful and capable of destroying the world if it were to perish twice.

sub_questions.text_english:
"Fire" and "Ice" are used in the poem as _______.
(A) similes
(B) metaphors
(C) repetition
(D) oxymorons
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'metaphors' is correct. In the poem, 'Fire' is used as a metaphor for human desire and passion, while 'Ice' is a metaphor for hatred and cold indifference. The poet does not say desire is 'like' fire — he directly equates them, making them metaphors and not similes. They are not oxymorons or examples of repetition.

sub_questions.text_english: Comment on the overall mood of the extract.

key_points: The overall mood of the extract is reflective, philosophical, and subtly ominous.

sub_questions.solution: The overall mood of the extract is reflective and philosophically ominous. The poet calmly contemplates the possible destruction of the world, drawing on personal experience. Despite the grave subject of the world's end, the tone remains measured and contemplative rather than fearful, giving the extract a deeply thoughtful and somewhat dark, introspective atmosphere.

sub_questions.text_english:
Extract (b): The leaves strain toward the glass / small twigs stiff with exertion / long-cramped boughs shuffling under the roof / like newly discharged patients / half-dazed, moving / to the clinic doors. (The Trees)

How does the comparison between the boughs and newly discharged patients contribute to the theme or message of the poem? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: The comparison emphasises the trees' slow, difficult movement toward freedom after being confined indoors
It reinforces the poem's theme of nature reclaiming its rightful place
The simile of discharged patients suggests both struggle and inevitable liberation

sub_questions.solution: The comparison of boughs to newly discharged patients reinforces the poem's central theme of nature's struggle to reclaim its freedom. Just as patients leave a clinic slowly and unsteadily after long confinement, the trees move haltingly after being kept indoors. This simile powerfully captures the difficulty of the process while affirming that nature's return to the wild is inevitable and unstoppable.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the sentence with the appropriate option.
The imagery and descriptions in the poem create a mood of ______________________.
(A) satisfaction and elation
(B) transition and uncertainty
(C) confusion and chaos
(D) pessimism and certainty
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'transition and uncertainty' is correct. The imagery of leaves straining toward glass, stiff twigs, and cramped boughs shuffling like half-dazed patients all suggest movement and change — nature is transitioning from confinement to freedom. The slow, uncertain movement of the trees and the simile of dazed patients both evoke a mood of ongoing transition and uncertain progress.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank with one word.
The stiff movement of the twigs in the above extract suggests the ______________ .
sub_questions.solution: The stiff movement of the twigs suggests the struggle or effort the trees are making to break free from their confined space indoors. The word 'stiff with exertion' in the poem indicates that the twigs are straining hard, working against their cramped conditions in an effort to reach the open air outside.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the poet describe the bough as 'shuffling'?

key_points: The poet describes the bough as 'shuffling' to indicate its slow, weak, and cramped movement after being confined indoors for a long time.

sub_questions.solution: The poet describes the bough as 'shuffling' to convey the slow, laboured, and unsteady movement of the branches that have been cramped indoors for a long time. Just like a person who shuffles their feet when weakened or confined, the long-cramped boughs move haltingly and awkwardly as they attempt to find their way out to freedom in the open air.

questions.text_english: Answer any four of the following five questions in 40–50 words each. (4×3=12)

questions.solution: Short answer literature questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.
questions.topic: Short Answer Questions — Prose and Poetry

sub_questions.text_english: What strategy did the mother adopt to teach the young seagull how to fly? (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)

key_points: The mother used food as a lure
She stood on a ledge below with a piece of fish, pretending to eat it
The hungry seagull, unable to resist, dived towards the food and instinctively began to fly

sub_questions.solution: The mother seagull adopted a clever strategy of using food as bait to teach the young seagull to fly. She stood on a ledge below him, holding a piece of fish in her beak and pretending to eat it. Unable to resist his hunger, the young seagull dived toward the food and, in doing so, instinctively spread his wings and began to fly for the first time.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the tiger in the zoo ignore the visitors? (A Tiger in the Zoo)

key_points: The tiger is imprisoned and has lost his natural freedom
He is helpless, resigned, and deeply dissatisfied with his confinement
Ignoring visitors is his silent protest and a sign of his broken spirit

sub_questions.solution: The tiger in the zoo ignores the visitors because he is deeply anguished by his captivity and has lost all hope of freedom. Confined to a small cage, far from his natural habitat, he is resigned and broken in spirit. Ignoring visitors is his silent act of protest and dignity — he refuses to perform or respond for their entertainment, symbolising suppressed rage and pride.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is the baker very important to the village folk? (Glimpses of India – A Baker from Goa)

key_points: The baker provides bread essential for all celebrations and festivals
Marriage feasts, engagement ceremonies, and festivals like Christmas cannot be celebrated without bread
The baker's role is deeply embedded in the cultural and social life of the Goan village

sub_questions.solution: The baker is extremely important to the village folk of Goa because he plays a central role in their social and cultural life. No celebration — whether a marriage feast, a birthday, or a festival like Christmas — is complete without bread and other baked goods. The baker's sweet bread, bonas, and bol are indispensable to Goan traditions, making him a beloved and essential part of village life.

sub_questions.text_english: Why did the poet not console the grief-stricken boy when he lost the ball? (The Ball Poem)

key_points: The poet wanted the boy to learn to cope with loss on his own
He believed the boy needed to understand the nature of responsibility and irretrievable loss
Consoling him would prevent him from learning this important life lesson

sub_questions.solution: The poet did not console the grief-stricken boy because he believed the boy needed to experience and learn from this loss on his own. The loss of the ball represents a boy's first encounter with irretrievable loss — something no money can buy back. The poet felt that consoling the boy would deprive him of the important life lesson of learning to cope with loss and responsibility.

sub_questions.text_english: Saving money for the bus journey was not easy for Valli. Explain. (Madam Rides the Bus)

key_points: Valli had to save sixty paise for the bus fare and the return journey
She resisted many temptations such as toys, snacks, and rides at the village fair
She saved carefully over a long period without telling her family

sub_questions.solution: Saving money for the bus journey was very difficult for Valli because she had to carefully set aside sixty paise — the fare for a one-way trip — without asking her family. She had to resist many tempting purchases such as peppermint candy, toys, and rides at the village fair. Over many months, through great self-discipline and secret saving, she finally managed to collect enough for the round trip.

questions.text_english: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40–50 words each. (2×3=6)
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40–50 words each.
questions.solution: Short answer literature questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Ausable get rid of Max? (The Midnight Visitor)

key_points: Ausable cleverly invented the story of a nonexistent balcony below his window
When a knock came at the door, Ausable said it was the police he had called
Max, fearing the police, stepped onto the supposed balcony and fell to his death

sub_questions.solution: Ausable got rid of Max through sheer cleverness and quick thinking. He invented a fictional balcony below his window, making Max believe it existed. When a knock came at the door, Ausable announced it was the police he had called. Fearing arrest, Max stepped backward toward the supposed balcony to escape but fell out of the window, as no balcony actually existed.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does Mme Loisel hastily depart from the ball when her husband places a modest wrap on her shoulders? (The Necklace)

key_points: Mme Loisel is deeply ashamed of her ordinary, modest wrap
She fears the rich women around her will notice how plain it is
She does not want the contrast between her borrowed finery and her real poverty to be exposed

sub_questions.solution: Mme Loisel hastily departs from the ball because she is deeply ashamed of her modest, ordinary wrap. After spending the evening in borrowed jewellery and a beautiful gown, mingling with wealthy and elegantly dressed women, she cannot bear the thought of her plain wrap revealing her true, humble social status. She rushes out to avoid being seen and judged by the fashionable crowd around her.

sub_questions.text_english: "In time you will be more learned than anyone else in the village. Then no one will ever be able to laugh at you." What effect did her teacher's words have on Bholi? Elaborate. (Bholi)

key_points: The teacher's words gave Bholi hope and a sense of purpose
She began to look forward to going to school and learning
The encouragement transformed her from a frightened, rejected girl into a confident and determined one

sub_questions.solution: The teacher's kind and encouraging words had a profound and transformative effect on Bholi. Until then, Bholi had been treated as a burden by her family and mocked by society due to her pockmarked face and slow speech. The teacher's words filled her with hope, self-belief, and a sense of purpose. She began to value education and grew into a confident, courageous young woman who later stood up against injustice.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100–120 words.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Long answer literature questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse and evaluate the role of faith in 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares'.

key_points: In 'A Letter to God,' Lencho's unshakeable faith in God drives the entire narrative
His faith is childlike and absolute — he believes God will send him money
Ironically, it is human kindness that fulfils his faith, but he suspects the post office workers of stealing
In 'The Sermon at Benares,' the Buddha uses faith and acceptance of impermanence to console the grief-stricken Kisa Gotami
Faith here is redirected from belief in miracles to acceptance of universal truth
Both texts show faith as a powerful force, though they present its outcomes differently

sub_questions.solution: Faith plays a central yet contrasting role in both 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares.' In 'A Letter to God,' Lencho's faith in God is absolute and unwavering. After a hailstorm destroys his crop, he writes directly to God asking for money, never doubting that God will respond. His faith is so strong that when the post office workers collectively send him money, he accepts it as God's gift but ironically suspects the workers of stealing the rest. His faith, though admirable, is blind and uncritical. In 'The Sermon at Benares,' faith takes a more mature and philosophical form. Kisa Gotami approaches the Buddha with desperate faith, hoping for a miracle to revive her dead son. The Buddha gently redirects her faith from denial to acceptance, teaching her that death and suffering are universal. Here, faith matures into wisdom. Both texts affirm that faith is a deeply human impulse, but while Lencho's faith remains rigid, Kisa Gotami's evolves into enlightenment.

sub_questions.text_english: Explore the contrasting images of the tiger in 'A Tiger in the Zoo' and the tiger in 'How to Tell Wild Animals'.

key_points: In 'A Tiger in the Zoo,' the tiger is shown as a captive, confined creature, stripped of his natural power
He paces restlessly in a small cage, his freedom lost, his spirit broken
In 'How to Tell Wild Animals,' the tiger is shown as fierce, powerful, and free in its natural habitat
The tiger in the poem leaps on people with yellow-and-black stripes clearly visible
The contrast highlights themes of captivity vs freedom and dignity vs suppression

sub_questions.solution: The two poems present sharply contrasting images of the tiger, offering very different perspectives on the animal. In 'A Tiger in the Zoo' by Leslie Norris, the tiger is portrayed as a captive creature stripped of his natural power and dignity. He paces restlessly in his narrow cage, quietly suffering. His eyes blaze with helpless rage as he stares at the brilliant stars — a poignant symbol of the freedom he can never reclaim. He ignores visitors, his silence a form of dignified protest against an unjust confinement. In contrast, the tiger in Carolyn Wells' humorous poem 'How to Tell Wild Animals' is presented as a magnificent, ferocious wild creature roaming freely. With his distinctive yellow-black stripes and powerful leap, he is described almost comically as the Bengal Tiger who will hug you — meaning attack — so tightly you'll know him. This tiger is wild, fearsome, and fully in command of his environment. Together, the two images form a powerful commentary on the difference between a tiger in his natural, free state and one reduced to pacing a zoo cage — highlighting the tragedy of captivity and the importance of preserving wildlife in the wild.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100–120 words.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Long answer supplementary reader questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Anil bring about a change in Hari Singh? (The Thief's Story)

key_points: Anil treated Hari Singh with trust and kindness without demanding anything in return
He taught Hari Singh to read, write, and cook — giving him skills and dignity
When Hari Singh stole his money, Anil pretended not to notice, giving him a chance to return it
Hari Singh returned the money, moved by Anil's trust and the realisation that education could give him a better future
Anil's silent forgiveness transformed Hari Singh's thinking about his life of crime

sub_questions.solution: Anil brought about a remarkable and deeply humane change in Hari Singh through trust, kindness, and the gift of education. When Hari Singh, a petty thief, befriended Anil under false pretences, Anil sensed something was amiss but chose to trust him anyway. He gave Hari Singh food, shelter, and most importantly, taught him to read and write — offering him the tools to build an honest future. When Hari Singh stole Anil's money one night and ran away, he was on the verge of escaping permanently. However, as he sat at the railway station with the stolen notes, he reflected on what Anil had given him — education, respect, and trust. He realised that a life of crime would only lead to emptiness, while literacy could open countless doors. Moved by guilt and gratitude, he returned the money before dawn. Anil, having noticed the damp notes, understood everything but chose to forgive silently. The next morning, he gave Hari Singh an advance on his wages and promised to pay him regularly. This silent act of forgiveness and continued faith transformed Hari Singh — making him recognise the value of an honest life over the fleeting gains of theft.

sub_questions.text_english: In what ways does Think-Tank misinterpret innocent nursery rhymes as threats to the Martians? (The Book That Saved the Earth)

key_points: Think-Tank interprets 'Mistress Mary' as evidence that Earthlings grow explosives in their gardens
He interprets 'Humpty Dumpty' as the Earthlings predicting his own downfall
He interprets 'Little Miss Muffet' as Earthlings training giant spiders as a weapon against Martians
Each misinterpretation reveals Think-Tank's arrogance and lack of understanding of human culture
His fear causes him to cancel the invasion of Earth

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Book That Saved the Earth,' Think-Tank, the pompous ruler of Mars, misinterprets innocent nursery rhymes from a book of children's poetry as dangerous threats to Martians. His misreadings are both humorous and revealing of his arrogance and foolishness. When Sergeant Oop reads 'Mistress Mary, Quite Contrary,' Think-Tank is convinced that Earthlings grow weapons — cockleshells and silver bells — in their gardens, indicating superior military technology. The rhyme 'Humpty Dumpty' terrifies him even more, as he believes it to be a prophecy foretelling his own downfall — Humpty Dumpty falls off a wall, and Think-Tank's head resembles a large round egg. He becomes convinced that the Earthlings know about him and have prepared for his defeat. Finally, 'Little Miss Muffet' leads him to believe that Earthlings have trained giant spiders as weapons to attack Martians. Each absurd misinterpretation escalates his paranoia. His comical terror leads him to cancel the planned invasion of Earth entirely and flee to the far reaches of the universe. The play brilliantly satirises arrogance and the danger of misunderstanding other cultures, while celebrating the power of books and literature in protecting civilisation.
